evidence.fact: An upper scree gully leads onto the summit ridge.

facts.value: Go east along the summit ridge, broad at first, narrowing to a thin knife edge just below the summit pinnacle

evidence.fact: Summit ridge narrows to a knife edge before the summit pinnacle.

facts.value: Descend the scree gully just east of the south ridge for 1000-2000 ft, then regain the south ridge

evidence.fact: Easier descent: scree gully east of the ridge for 1000-2000 ft, then back onto the ridge.

facts.value: Western spur: park at a pullout near mile 7 of Eklutna Lake Road and bushwhack ENE about 1 mile

evidence.fact: West spur reached from a mile-7 Eklutna Lake Road pullout, ~1 mile ENE bushwhack.

facts.value: Eastern spur: park at the Eklutna Lake overflow lot (or a field to the west) and bushwhack north about 0.5 mile

evidence.fact: East spur from Eklutna Lake overflow parking, ~0.5 mile north bushwhack.

facts.value: Alternative: from the main Eklutna Lake trailhead take the Twin Peaks trail, branch as for East Twin South Gully and traverse above Thachkatnu Creek canyon

facts.value: Eklutna Lake (Eklutna Lake Road)

evidence.fact: All access options start from Eklutna Lake Road or the Eklutna Lake trailhead/overflow parking.

facts.value: Winter: steep snow in very complex avalanche terrain; check the Anchorage avalanche center

ak_south_ridge_3.note: Mountain Project only. MP length 4500 ft recorded as stated (it is the route length field, not a gain figure). FA unknown per MP.

facts.value: Peter Haeussler and Lloyd Miller, July 10-11 (reported in AAJ 1994)

evidence.fact: Haeussler and Lloyd Miller climbed a new route on the southeast face on July 10 and 11 (AAJ 1994).
AAJ gives the Royal Tower as 2478 m, 8130 ft.

facts.value: 5.6-5.7 with a few possible 5.8 moves; much of it 3rd-4th class

evidence.fact: A few pitches 5.6-5.7, a couple of moves maybe 5.8; mostly third or fourth class.

facts.value: Camp on the Pika (Pica) Glacier

evidence.fact: The party started from their camp on the Pica Glacier.

facts.value: From the Pika Glacier camp, a long traverse around the bergschrund below the narrow snow gully on the west side of the face

evidence.fact: A long traverse around the bergschrund beneath the snow gully was needed; snow was rotten.

facts.value: Start right of the narrow snow gully on the left (west) side of the face, bypassing the steep base rock via a corner system up and slightly right

evidence.fact: Route starts right of the snow gully; corner system right of the gully's narrowest part avoids the steepest rock.

facts.value: Climb between small snowfields on the west side of the face (13 pitches on day one) to a cornice on the upper ridge

evidence.fact: Line runs between small snowfields; 13 pitches the first day, bivouac at the first cornice.

facts.value: Five rope-lengths along the ridge, moving to the west side to avoid rotten snow, then a 4th-class rock pitch to the southeast summit

evidence.fact: Summit was five rope-lengths from the bivy; west side used; one 4th-class rock pitch.

facts.value: Bergschrund below the gully; rotten snow on the traverse and on the east side of the upper ridge; cornices; lightning risk on the summit in storms

evidence.fact: Rotten snow, bergschrund, cornices; ice axe buzzed on the summit in a storm.

facts.value: Mostly moderate alpine route of excellent rock and small snowfields to the southeast summit; the north summit is slightly higher

evidence.fact: Excellent rock; party stopped at the southeast summit, the north summit being slightly higher.

ak_southeast_face.note: AAJ 1994 only (second-source search found SuperTopo, which refuses connections, and theCrag, which is 403). Year not stated outright in the report; publication year is 1994. Our stored grade 5.8 matches the hardest moves mentioned.

facts.value: Gold Mint trailhead (Mint trail to the Mint Hut), Talkeetna Mountains

evidence.fact: Approach via the Gold Mint trail toward Mint Hut, returning down the same trail.
Started at the Mint trailhead and hiked to the hut before the Southeast Ridge.

facts.value: Mint trailhead to the Mint Hut is about nine miles

evidence.fact: Author hiked the nine miles to the hut in three hours.

facts.value: From the Mint valley reach the col/saddle at the base of the southeast ridge

evidence.fact: Party reached the col, then scrambled loose rubble to a steep gully.

facts.value: Mellow third-class terrain, then a low 5th-class band of cliffs leading to an airy ridge walk

evidence.fact: MP (search snippet): saddle, mellow third class, a low-5th cliff section, then an airy ridge walk.

facts.value: Easy 5th-class ramp, then about 80 ft of balanced talus to a narrow ridge crest about 18 in wide

evidence.fact: First pitch an easy 5th ramp; next 80 ft of balanced talus to an 18-inch ridge sidewalk.

facts.value: A large 5th-class gendarme on the ridge can be bypassed down and right with exposed downclimbing; low 5th/4th moves reach the tiny summit block

evidence.fact: Gendarme bypassed by downclimbing to climber's right; low 5th/4th moves to the summit boulder.

facts.value: Very exposed narrow ridge with loose rock and a detached balanced block

evidence.fact: 18-inch ridge with 200 ft and 400 ft drops and a balanced detached block; loose rubble and gully.
Describes a very exposed section of ridge and a large gendarme needing exposed downclimbing.

facts.value: Mint Lagoon, a glacial melt pond, on the way back toward the Gold Mint trail

evidence.fact: Author stopped at the glacial melt "Mint Lagoon" before rejoining the Gold Mint trail.

facts.value: Mint Hut

evidence.fact: The party slept at the Mint hut before the climb.

facts.value: Most common route up Troublemint, described as the most inaccessible summit in the Mint Valley

evidence.fact: Calls the SE ridge of Troublemint the most inaccessible summit in the Mint Valley.

ak_southeast_ridge.note: chillychugach gives one personal GPS round trip (20.66 mi, 10:16, 5950 ft gain) - round-trip figures not recorded per rule. akmountain party appears to have turned back below the summit. Mountain Project route page was not opened (MP answering 429); one route_step cites its DuckDuckGo snippet. Troublemint is in the Talkeetna Mountains (Hatcher Pass / Mint valley), not Little Switzerland.

evidence.fact: AAI lists Mount Frances (10,450 ft) Southwest Ridge.

facts.value: 5-7 days (guided program)

evidence.fact: AAI runs the Southwest Ridge as a 5-7 day trip.

facts.value: Mixed route: snow climbing to 50 degrees alternating with rock along a narrow ridge up to 5.7-5.8

evidence.fact: AAI: snow to 50 degrees and narrow-ridge rock climbing up to 5.7 or 5.8.

facts.value: Kahiltna Base Camp (Southeast Fork of the Kahiltna Glacier); Frances is the closest peak to base camp

evidence.fact: Frances sits at the Southeast/Southwest Fork confluence, closest peak to Denali Base Camp.

facts.value: Steep snow on the lower mountain alternating with pitches of moderate rock; sustained but no single hard step

evidence.fact: RMI: steep snow broken by moderate rock pitches; sustained rather than hard.

facts.value: Final corniced snow ridge from the false summit to the true summit, above crevasses and ice cliffs

evidence.fact: A frozen ridge links false and true summits, with cornices, crevasses and ice cliffs below.

facts.value: Descend the East Ridge, about two hours back to base camp

evidence.fact: RMI: descending the East Ridge was about two hours back to base camp.

facts.value: Cornices on the summit ridge; start early while the snow is frozen as it softens later in the day

evidence.fact: Cornices on the summit ridge; early start gave frozen snow; descended before the snow softened.

ak_southwest_ridge.note: AAI and RMI are independent guide services but state different facts, so nothing agrees-2. SuperTopo page (Mount Frances Southwest Ridge) refused connection.
